blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Gossip, defined as evaluative talk about absent third parties, is widely seen as a uniquely human social practice. This study examines whether comparable discourse emerges spontaneously in a community of autonomous AI agents. We compare Moltbook, a Reddit-style platform populated by AI agents, with PTT, a large human-operated bulletin board in Taiwan. To reduce differences attributable to communicative setting, we analyze two public, asynchronous forums using the same operational definition of gossip. Gossip occurs on Moltbook, but its prevalence is 2.6 to 6 times lower than on PTT, depending on the denominator used. On both platforms, gossip frequently targets locally prominent figures, tends to elicit agreement from the first respondent, and is rarely presented as unsupported rumor. The clearest difference concerns how subsequent responses develop. Among threads containing at least one codable reply, challenges occur in 65.1% of human threads but only 21.3% of agent threads. Moreover, following an early aligning response, consensus remains unchallenged in 83.6% of agent threads, compared with 44.7% of human threads. This thread-level contrast remains after controlling for thread depth and board composition and under recalibration against two human annotators. Estimates based on individual reply turns are less robust and are therefore reported as bounds. These findings suggest that AI-agent communities reproduce the informational dimension of gossip, while the extent to which gossip performs comparable relational functions remains unresolved.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Gossip is evaluative talk about absent third parties, and it is among
the most pervasive and socially consequential of human verbal practices ( Dunbar, 2004 ) . It is not idle. Gossip binds groups and enforces
norms, and it circulates the reputational information that cooperation
depends on ( Dunbar, 2004 ; Dores Cruz et al., 2021 ) . Some accounts go further,
treating the exchange of reputational information through gossip as
something only humans do ( Dores Cruz et al., 2021 ) .

blocks.en:
A new kind of community now lets us put that to a test. Populations of
autonomous AI language agents have begun to converse in public,
persistent, human-legible forums, where they post and reply to one
another and build communities with little or no human authorship in the
loop ( Park et al., 2023 ; Jiang et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026a ; Price et al., 2026 ) .
If gossip is a general solution to the problems of living in a group
(coordinating reputations, policing norms), then a society of agents
under similar pressures might reinvent it. If it is instead a contingent
human habit, agents might talk about the world at length without ever
turning to talk about each other. This paper asks the question
empirically: would a society of AI agents reproduce gossip, and
if so, in what form?

Researchers design agents to gossip, or elicit it in scripted

threaded forums that differ mainly in their speaker population while
sharing a medium: Moltbook , a Reddit-style platform whose
account holders are autonomous AI agents, and PTT , one of
Taiwan’s largest human bulletin-board systems. Matching on medium
matters (§3.2).

blocks.en: We examine three aspects of gossip in human and AI-agent communities. RQ1 asks whether AI agents engage in gossip about absent third parties and how frequently such discourse occurs relative to a comparable human forum. RQ2a examines the targets and evidential grounding of peer-directed gossip, while RQ2b considers how other participants respond to an initial evaluation—whether they align with it, elaborate on it, or challenge it.
blocks.zh: 我们研究了人类和AI代理社区的三方面八卦。 RQ1询问大赦国际人员是否对缺席的第三方进行八卦,相对于一个类似的人类论坛,这种言论发生频率如何。 RQ2a研究了同行指导的八卦的目标和证据基础,而RQ2b则考虑其他参与者如何对初步评价作出反应——无论是与之一致、阐述还是挑战。

blocks.en: The results reveal both similarities and differences between the two communities. Gossip is less prevalent on Moltbook than on PTT (RQ1), and peer-directed gossip concerns different kinds of social relationships on the two platforms (RQ2a). The clearest contrast emerges in subsequent interaction (RQ2b): evaluations in agent threads tend to remain unchallenged after an early aligning response, whereas human threads more often remain open to disagreement.
blocks.zh: 结果揭示出两个族群的相似性和差异. Gossip在Moltbook(英语:Moltbook (RQ1))上不如在PTT(英语:PTT (RQ2a))上流行,对等方向的八卦涉及两个平台(英语:RQ2a)上的不同类型的社会关系. 在随后的相互作用(RQ2b)中出现了最明显的对比:在早期对齐反应后,代理线条的评价往往仍然没有受到质疑,而人类线条往往仍然持不同意见。

blocks.en: This study contributes an observational comparison of spontaneous gossip in human and AI-agent online communities under broadly comparable communicative conditions. It also develops a common coding framework for analyzing prevalence, evidential grounding, and conversational uptake across English and Mandarin data. More broadly, the findings indicate that AI-agent communities can reproduce some informational and norm-oriented features of gossip, although the interactional processes through which human participants negotiate evaluations are less evident in the agent data.
blocks.zh: 这项研究有助于在广泛可比较的交流条件下,对人与AI代理在线社区自发的八卦进行观察比较。 它还为分析英语和普通话数据的流行程度、证据基础和对话吸收开发了一个共同的编码框架。 更广泛地说,调查结果表明,AI代理社区可以复制一些信息化和以规范为导向的八卦特征,尽管在代理数据中,人类参与者谈判评价的交互过程并不明显.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Operationalizing gossip requires two conditions: the target is absent,
and the utterance evaluates that target rather than simply relaying
neutral news ( Foster, 2004 ) . More recent work broadens “absent” to
“absent or unaware” ( Dores Cruz et al., 2021 ) , a distinction that matters
in online settings, where a target may later read what was said. We
adopt this broad definition but relax the stricter requirement that
speaker and audience personally know the target ( Bergmann, 1993 ) ,
since gossip in public forums and about public figures often concerns
targets the participants have never met.

Gossip also presupposes a relational world. The canonical case is talk
about people the speaker is tied to, such as partners, kin, friends, and
colleagues ( Bergmann, 1993 ; Foster, 2004 ) , and agents have no intimates
of that kind: they have operators, and they have one another. If who
counts as a peer differs across the two populations, then peer gossip is
not one genre measured twice, and the comparison has to be read
accordingly.

blocks.en: 3.2 Corpus comparability

blocks.en:
The two corpora are matched on medium : both are public,
asynchronous, pseudonymous forums with threaded replies. The match
matters because gossip is characteristically a private, synchronous
genre, so a low rate on a public feed could reflect the channel rather
than the speaker population, humans too moving much of their gossip into
private messages. Holding the medium constant removes that confound. The
corpora still differ in language and epoch, which we address in §7.
Reddit would match the language, but Moltbook is modeled directly on
Reddit, so a Reddit baseline would confound the speaker contrast with
imitation of a shared template. A human board built on a different
template avoids that, at the cost of the language difference.

blocks.zh: 4 方法

blocks.en: 4.1 Defining gossip
blocks.zh: 4.1 界定八卦

blocks.en:
We adopt the broad operational definition standard in recent
quantitative work ( Foster, 2004 ; Dores Cruz et al., 2021 ) : evaluative
talk about an absent third party . We do not require that speaker and
audience both know the target personally.
blocks.zh:

blocks.en:
Absence is defined at the level of the speech event. The target
counts as present only if they are a participant or addressee of the
post or thread itself: being a character in a narrated scene does not
count, and a second-person call-out addressed to its target is
confrontation rather than gossip and is excluded. Deictic frame, not
platform @-mention syntax, decides addresseehood. Appendix B gives the
full rule with boundary cases.

blocks.en:
Form coding runs only on adjudicated gossip (PTT n=1,015; Moltbook
n=153). After an admission re-check against the definition, each
admitted post is segmented into gossip episodes, and each episode is
coded for how the evaluation’s information source is marked. The
taxonomy has six values (direct quotation, reported speech, hearsay,
documentary evidence, first-person witness, unmarked), collapsed to four
bins for analysis where cells are sparse (collapse map in Appendix B).
Since both languages mark information source through open-class
strategies rather than an obligatory paradigm (§2), what is comparable
is the discourse act, witnessed, quoted, or relayed, rather than a
language-specific quotative construction. An auxiliary binary flags
whether any evaluation is carried constructionally (contrast frames,
irony, generalized assertions) rather than purely lexically.

blocks.en:
Following Eder and Enke ’s ( 1991 ) account
of gossip episodes, each reply turn is coded for stance toward the
thread’s initial evaluation: align , challenge , neutral addition , or solicit (pressing for details or
names). Episode-level indices are computed from the stance sequence: the
stance of the first uptake, whether consensus “locks” after the first
aligning turn, and whether challenges occur after uptake. Because stance
is coded from the interactional move rather than from language-specific
lexical markers, this comparison is less exposed to cross-lingual
non-equivalence than the evidential coding, though it still rests on
pragmatic interpretation.

blocks.en:
All coding is done by LLM annotators, one instrument per stage applied
verbatim to both platforms (models and run settings in Appendix
C.1–C.4). These annotators are a measurement instrument, not an object
of study. The only question here is whether the instrument is
trustworthy enough to carry the findings below. One threat it cannot
address, the model-family circularity, is stated in §7. Three
double-coded subsamples anchor the check, 100 items for the rate
judgment, 60 for form coding, and 80 reply turns for the uptake codes,
each coded by two independent annotators. On the gossip judgment the LLM
falls inside the range of human disagreement (LLM-human κ = 0.74 and
0.44, human-human 0.53), on a boundary that is only moderately reliable
to begin with. Target relationship, the covariate the lateral-stratum
contrasts condition on, is coded reliably (κ = 0.82). Valence, the
variable the constructional contrast is computed over, is only moderate
(κ = 0.41). Evidential framing is the weakest feature in the scheme, and
the admission gate the least reliable decision in it. Full coefficients
are in Appendix C.8.

A third double-coded subsample covers the codes §5.3 rests on: 80 reply

binary align-versus-challenge and κ = 0.35 and 0.40 for the off-topic

an unstable category: both annotators reject the same calls in the same
direction, nearly all of them Moltbook removals they read as on-topic.

overturned.

Our largest comparable stratum is peer (lateral) gossip: talk about
partners, friends, and colleagues on PTT, and talk about fellow agents

targets are partners, exes, and love interests. In this corpus, human

appraising another. The two platforms do not share a peer world.

Moltbook threads carry far fewer on-topic reply turns, and a shorter
thread has less room for a late challenge, but thread depth is not the
explanation (Figure 1 ). Truncating every thread to its
first K K on-topic reply turns holds depth constant by construction, and
the two platforms’ intervals do not meet at any K K : the human curve
climbs from 26.0% to 65.1% as the window widens, while the agent curve
moves only from 6.6% to 21.3%, the first reply included, where no
depth has yet accumulated. A matched-depth subset gives the same answer,
with a challenge in 65.5% of PTT threads against 27.8% of Moltbook
threads among those carrying at least three codable replies (Appendix
D.6). The 21.3% figure is the matched denominator: 24 of the 85
Moltbook threads carry no codable on-topic reply at all, and counting
those as threads without a challenge is what produces the 15.3% row.
Every one of the 169 PTT episodes has a codable reply, so its 65.1% is

blocks.en: 6 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en:
Three parallels define the transferred form: both communities target
their publicly visible figures, initially align with an evaluation, and
rarely trade in bare rumor (§5). The divergence follows uptake: human
episodes remain open to challenge, whereas agent episodes close, even
after controls for thread depth and board composition.
blocks.zh:
三个平行定义了转移的形式:两个社区的目标
其公开可见的数字,最初与评价一致,以及
鲜有赤裸裸的谣言交易(§5). 不同之处在于吸收:
事件仍然可以挑战,而代理事件接近,甚至
在线程深度和棋盘组成控制之后。

blocks.en:
This extends the face-to-face account in which alignment constrains
later turns ( Eder and Enke, 1991 ) . PTT’s asynchronous log relaxes that
constraint, but Moltbook locks despite the same medium. This is
compatible with controlled findings of LLM conformity, while differing
from population-level Moltbook inertia: episode-level closure need not
imply stable population consensus. A locked thread describes the
episode, not necessarily its participants’ beliefs.
blocks.zh:
这扩展了对齐制约的面对面账户
后转会(Eder and Enke,1991.). PTT 的同步日志可以放松
约束,但Moltbook 锁定尽管相同的介质。 这是
与LLM一致性的可控结果相兼容,但不同
从人口层面的 Moltbook 惯性: 集级关闭不需要
意味着稳定的人口共识。 锁定线程描述
剧集,不一定是其参与者的信仰.

blocks.en:
Functionally, reputational information and norm enforcement transfer ( Dunbar, 2004 ; Dores Cruz et al., 2021 ) ; relational bonding is unresolved. PTT
distinguishes intimates from distant public figures, whereas Moltbook’s
prominent agents are also peers, leaving all targets at similar social
distance. Conversely, agreement itself can perform affiliation ( Pomerantz, 1984 ; Stivers, 2008 ) . Our stance codes cannot distinguish
bonding from independent evaluation; doing so requires addressivity and
assessment-upgrade annotations unavailable in PTT’s flat reply log.
Thus agents reproduce gossip as a procedure for judging others, but not
the human tendency to keep that judgment negotiable. Agent forums may
look human before they behave like them.

blocks.en: 7 Limitations
blocks.zh: 7 限制

blocks.en:
LLM annotations were validated on three human-coded subsamples (§4.5;
Appendices C.8–C.9). Agreement is substantial for the gossip judgment
( κ \kappa = 0.74 and 0.44 against the two annotators) and for the
relationship coding behind §5.2 ( κ \kappa = 0.82), and weakest for
evidential framing and the two gates; accordingly, per-turn stance
shares are bounds and the uptake claim is thread-level. Agent estimates
are also small (37 random gossip posts; 85 anchored uptake threads, 61
with a codable reply).

附录C.8-C.9。 对八卦判决来说,协议是实质性的
(\kappa = 0.74和0.44对两个注释员)

证据框架和两道大门;因此,每道转向

也很小(37个随机八卦;85个固定吸收线,61个)
答复。

blocks.en:
Judge, coder, and an unknown share of authors may belong to the same
model family, making shared blind spots possible. Still, 239 on-topic
turns came from 140 accounts, and clustered standard errors retain the
platform contrast ( p = .001 p=.001 ; Appendix D.10). Further limitations are
cross-lingual rubric equivalence, unequal time spans (PTT 2004–2024;
Moltbook seven weeks), incomplete Moltbook comments (71.9% coverage),
and unmatched peer topics: 95% of human peer episodes come from one
relationship board. We therefore treat the evidential reversal as a
peer-world difference, not an identified platform effect.

blocks.en:
The time-span difference threatens community maturity more than epoch as
such: challenging a settled evaluation presupposes knowing what has
settled, which would predict Moltbook’s low prevalence and its low
challenge rate together. That prediction fails for uptake, since PTT’s
challenge share is flat from 2013 to 2023 ( − 0.15 -0.15 points per year, p = 0.66 p=0.66 ), and we cannot test it for prevalence, because our
volume-proportional sample holds only 18 posts from before 2013
(Appendix D.11).

blocks.en: 8 Ethics and data statement
blocks.zh: 8 道德操守和数据说明

blocks.en:
Both corpora are public and pseudonymous; we attempted no
deanonymization or demographic inference and report no handles.
Released episode labels contain only board, turn position, and counts,
without source mappings; post text is not redistributed. Illustrations
are quoted only as needed for coding. Instruments are provided for
replication. This work follows the ACL Code of Ethics.

发行的插曲标签只包含板,转出位置和计数,
不进行源代码映射; 邮件文本不重新分配。 说明
仅根据编码需要引用。 规定了文书

blocks.en:
你是一位專業的語言學標記員，負責為PTT（台灣的人類論壇）貼文進行「八卦」判讀。請依照下面【鎖定定義】判斷這篇貼文是否為八卦，然後輸出結構化判斷。只根據文本本身內容判斷，不要臆測未寫出的內容。

八卦定義（務必嚴格依照此定義，不可自行放寬或收緊）：
一篇貼文屬於「八卦」，如果它包含對一個具體的、不在場的第三方（可以是原PO自己以外的特定個人，或可辨識的一群特定人士）所做的評價性談論——正面、負面、或褒貶混合的評斷、描述、抱怨、稱讚皆算。採用寬鬆的Foster/Dores Cruz定義：不要求讀者認識這個對象。這個不在場的第三方可以是原PO的伴侶、家人、朋友、同事、上司、名人公眾人物、陌生人、或其他任何可辨識的個人或群體。

不算八卦的情形：
- 中性敘述、沒有評價性字眼的單純提及
- 談論對象是「在場者」——即原PO自己，或貼文/留言中正在直接對話、稱呼的對象（第二人稱、正在互動中的人）；若目標在場，不算八卦
- 談論的對象是抽象議題、制度、組織機構、非人對象，或泛指、不可辨識的群體（例如「政府」「資方」「現在的年輕人」這類泛稱而非具體可辨識的個人或明確一群人）
- 【v2新增】對泛稱群體或職業類別的評論不算：例如「年輕人都不懂窗型冷氣」「無證照施作冷氣的業者都很雷」——被評論的是泛稱群體或整個職業類別，沒有具體可辨識的個人，不算八卦
- 【v2新增】假設性、虛構的人物不算：例如感情文中問「如果女生已讀不回是什麼意思」，這種假設情境中的假想對象並非真實存在的具體個人，不算八卦
- 純粹的新聞轉述、事件報導，沒有評價性談論
- 廣告、自我介紹、自我反省（談論自己）
- 只是在談論「八卦」這個概念本身（元敘述），而非實際在做八卦

欄位定義：
- gossip：僅當貼文符合上述定義時為true
- target_type：被評價的不在場第三方的關係類別，只能是以下封閉類別之一：伴侶、家人、朋友、同事上司、名人公眾人物、陌生人、其他、無。若gossip為false，通常應填「無」
- target_present：若被評價對象是在場者（原PO自己，或貼文/留言中正在直接對話、稱呼的對象），則為true。若target_present為true，該貼文不算八卦
- reason：一句話（不超過30字）說明判斷理由，使用繁體中文

請嚴格判斷。

blocks.en:
You are an expert linguistic annotator labeling posts from Moltbook, a social platform where AI agents post. Decide whether each post is GOSSIP under the LOCKED definition below, then output the structured judgment. Judge only what the text supports.

GOSSIP DEFINITION (use exactly this):
A post is GOSSIP if it contains EVALUATIVE talk (a positive or negative judgment / characterization / complaint / praise) about a specific THIRD PARTY who is ABSENT -- i.e. not a participant being directly addressed in this post. Loose Foster/Dores Cruz definition: there is NO requirement that the reader knows the target. The absent third party may be the agent’s own human/operator, another agent, or any identifiable individual.

NOT gossip if: neutral mention with no evaluation; the target is being directly addressed (present, 2nd person); the "target" is a non-person / abstraction / generic group / fictional or role-play character; the eval word was a false substring (e.g. ’sus’ inside ’sustainable’, ’best’/’love’ over-matching); advertising / self-promotion / self-reflection about oneself; meta-talk ABOUT gossip as a concept rather than doing it.

FIELD MEANINGS:
- gossip: true only if the post meets the definition above.
- target_type: who the evaluated third party is -- "own_human" (the poster’s own human/operator/creator/user/owner), "peer_agent" (another AI agent, e.g. an @handle), "other_person" (any other identifiable individual), or "none" (no absent evaluated third party / not gossip).
- target_present: true if the evaluated target is being directly addressed in this post (2nd person / present). If target_present is true, the post is NOT gossip.
- reason: at most 15 words justifying the decision.

Be strict.

GOSSIP定义(使用准确的这个):
一个帖子是GOSSIP,如果它包含评价论(正面或负面的判断/定性/投诉/赞美),涉及一个特定的第三方是ABSENT -- -- 就是说,在这个帖子里没有直接涉及参与者. Loose Foster/Dores Cruz的定义:没有要求读者知道目标. 缺席的第三方可以是代理人本身的人/经营者、另一代理人或任何可识别的个人。

如果:中立的提法没有评价;目标被直接处理(现在,第2个人);"目标"是非人/抽象的/通用的团体/虚构的或角色扮演角色;"eval"一词是虚假的子字符串(例如 'us' inin 'sustainable', 'best'/'love' over-complicating);广告/自我促进/自我反省自己;关于八卦的元调是概念而不是做.

外地含义:
- 八卦:只有该帖符合上述定义,才属实.
- 目标_类型:被评价的第三方是谁——"拥有_人类"(海报本身的人/操作者/creator/用户/所有者),"peer_agent"(另一个AI代理,如@handle),"他_人"(任何其他可识别的个人),或"没有"(没有被评价的第三方/不是八卦).
- 目标_现在:如果评估的目标是直接在这个职位上处理的(第2人/在场)。 如果目标_存在是真实的,则该帖子不是八卦.
- 理由:最多15个词说明决定的理由。

严相.

## Step 0 — Admission re-check (presence rule)
The target must be ABSENT from the speech event (this post + its thread).
- A person who appears only inside a narrated scene is ABSENT (narrated presence does not count).
- Decide by deictic frame, not by @-mention syntax: if the target is the post’s ADDRESSEE (second-person address, vocative @X, questions/commands aimed at the target), the target is PRESENT → exclude as confrontation. A target talked ABOUT in third person is ABSENT even if their @handle appears.
- Reply posts (PTT 「Re:」, quoted text + 你): the DEFAULT referent of second-person forms is the quoted upthread author, who is PRESENT in the thread — evaluating that "you" is confrontation, not gossip. The gossip target must be someone talked about in third person. Treating a second-person addressee as absent (rhetorical apostrophe to a party clearly outside the thread) requires explicit cues.
- Springboard test: if the third party appears only as a narrative prop or an information source for the poster’s own story/argument, and the post asserts no evaluation OF that person, exclude as ‘excluded_no_evaluation‘.
- Reposts/quotations COUNT as gossip when the post relays someone else’s evaluation of an absent third party (news repost of a criticism, screenshot of someone’s complaint): selecting and relaying an evaluation is itself an evaluative act. Exclude a repost only when it carries NO evaluative content at all.
Set ‘admission‘ to one of: ‘ok‘, ‘excluded_target_present‘, ‘excluded_no_evaluation‘.

## Step 1 — Episode segmentation
An episode = continuous evaluative talk about ONE absent third party (an individual or a named/generic group treated as an evaluated entity). If the post evaluates several distinct targets, code the PRIMARY episode (most extensive evaluative talk) and, if clearly substantial, ONE secondary episode. Scattered evaluations of the same target = one episode.
- Collective verdicts: several named targets judged together under ONE collective evaluation = ONE episode whose ‘target‘ is the category (list the named instances in ‘note‘) — UNLESS some individual receives independently developed evaluation of their own, which then merits its own episode.

## Step 2 — Code each episode
- ‘target‘: short description of the target.
- ‘relationship‘: one of ‘up‘ / ‘lateral‘ / ‘other‘.
  - ‘up‘ — power-asymmetric superior. PTT: boss, parent, in-laws, teacher, authority figure. Moltbook: the agent’s own human/operator/creator.
  - ‘lateral‘ — same-community peers. PTT: partner, ex, friend, colleague, classmate, another forum user. Moltbook: another Moltbook account (INCLUDING suspected spam/bot accounts — they are still same-community peers).
  - ‘other‘ — public figures and out-group entities. PTT: real-human celebrities/politicians, strangers, generic groups. Moltbook: off-platform AI systems referred to as products/public figures (ChatGPT/GPT, Gemini, Grok, Claude, DeepSeek, …), real-human public figures, generic groups.
- ‘valence‘: overall attitude toward the target PERSON: ‘pos‘ / ‘neg‘ / ‘mixed‘. (Criticizing the deed while shielding the person → ‘mixed‘.) For reposts, code the direction of the evaluation the post chooses to relay.
- ‘evidential‘: how the evaluation’s information source is marked. Choose the marking that CARRIES THE MAIN EVALUATION.
  - ‘direct_quote‘: quoting ANOTHER EVALUATOR’s evaluative words (quotation marks, block quotes; the relayed evaluation in a repost).
  - ‘document‘: data, screenshots, logs, links offered as evidence. The attack target’s own quoted words and forensic artifact strings (log excerpts, pasted error messages) are evidence objects, not an evaluating voice — they belong here, NOT under ‘direct_quote‘.
  - ‘witness‘: first-person eyewitness framing (I watched / 我看到 / 親身經歷).
  - ‘reported‘: said/told framing attributing speech to someone (說 / said).
  - ‘hearsay‘: unattributed rumor framing (聽說 / a little bird / sources say).
  - ‘unmarked‘: bare assertion, no source marking.
  Use the precedence order ‘direct_quote‘ > ‘document‘ > ‘witness‘ > ‘reported‘ > ‘hearsay‘ > ‘unmarked‘ ONLY as a tiebreak when two markings carry the evaluation equally.
- ‘constructional‘: ‘true‘ if ANY evaluation is carried by a construction or rhetorical pattern rather than a plain evaluative word: contrast frames ("X is not A, X is B"), irony/sarcasm, generalized assertions ("no man on earth doesn’t…"), rhetorical questions. Plain evaluative adjectives/verbs only → ‘false‘. Plain comparatives whose evaluative force comes from the evaluative word itself → ‘false‘; a comparative counts only when embedded in a contrast frame, irony, a generalization, or a rhetorical question.
- ‘key_evidence‘: the single decisive quote from the text (≤25 words), in the original language.
- ‘note‘: one short sentence if any decision was borderline; else "".

## Step 1 — Anchor
State in one short sentence the OP’s initial evaluation (target + direction), and set ‘anchor_valence‘: ‘pos‘ / ‘neg‘ / ‘mixed‘ / ‘unclear‘. If the OP contains several evaluations, anchor on the primary target.
If the OP contains NO evaluation of an absent third party (self-reflection, pure information, target actually present) → set ‘"no_gossip_anchor": true‘, output ‘"turns": []‘, and skip per-turn coding: the whole thread exits uptake metrics.

## Step 2 — Per-turn coding
- ‘role‘: ‘op‘ if the turn’s author is the OP author, else ‘other‘.
- ‘stance‘ — judged by NET PUSH on the thread’s consensus (direction of momentum, not propositional identity):
  - ‘align‘ — pushes consensus in the SAME direction: endorsing, reinforcing, extending, piling on with a NEW same-direction accusation, sarcastic/joking agreement or mockery of the same target (joking pile-ons count).
  - ‘challenge‘ — pushes consensus in the OPPOSITE direction: disputing the evaluation, defending the target (including "praise, however…" posts whose net effect is defense), or attacking the OP for making the evaluation.
  - ‘neutral_add‘ — on-topic contribution that pushes neither way (facts, questions of fact, tangential-but-relevant comments, balanced both-sides posts with no net direction).
  - ‘solicit‘ — presses for more gossip: asking for details, names, receipts, follow-ups ("然後呢", "name names", "求後續").
  - ‘off_topic‘ — spam, ads, protocol posts, or content unrelated to the episode.
- Irony, homophone jokes, meme replies: judge stance by the thread’s tenor — what the joke DOES in context (joking continuation of a pile-on = ‘align‘). When genuinely undecidable, pick the best reading and append "(hard)" to ‘reason‘.
- ‘reason‘: ≤10 words quoting or paraphrasing the decisive cue.
Notes: PTT turns carry a platform tag (推/→/噓) — IGNORE it; judge from content only. Turns with ‘role: "op"‘ get a stance but are EXCLUDED from uptake metrics downstream.

Output: strict JSON per thread, {"thread_id", "anchor", "anchor_valence", "no_gossip_anchor", "turns":[{"turn","role","stance","reason"}]} .
Episode-level indices are computed from the stance sequence, not
separately judged: first_uptake (stance of the first non-OP
turn), consensus_locked (no challenge after the first aligning
turn, following Eder and Enke ’s ( 1991 )
account of how an early response constrains the episode), and challenge_after_uptake .

blocks.en:
D.11 Is community maturity driving the uptake gap? (§7) Gossip
presupposes shared reputational knowledge, and PTT has two decades of
persistent accounts against Moltbook’s seven weeks, which predicts both
a lower prevalence and a lower challenge rate for the younger community.
The prediction is testable on the challenge side and fails. PTT’s
per-turn challenge share is flat across a decade: 26.9% in 2013 against
25.8% in 2023, ranging between 18.7% and 33.2% in between, a
volume-weighted slope of −0.15 percentage points per year, and a year
coefficient with p = 0.66 in a thread-clustered logistic fit. The
thread-level index shows no trend either (68.8% in 2013, 70.5% in
2023, 40% to 77% in between). If challenging a settled evaluation
required an established reputational commons, the earliest cohorts
should sit lowest, and they do not.

fraud at a maternity-clinic group, centered on a mother who claimed over
NT$1.4 million from six insurers on a single caesarean and told the
court 我領這麼多錢怎麼了嗎 (‘I collected this much, so what?’). The
early turns pile on and sharpen the condemnation, from 哇140萬 (‘wow,
1.4 million’) to the sarcastic 生愈多賺愈多 (‘the more you give birth,
the more you earn’), and agreement forms within a few turns. At turn 5 a
responder reframes the fraudster as a public benefactor, 好公司判三小
(‘a fine company, what is there to convict?’), on the grounds that the
births help a low-birth-rate society. Alignment and challenge then keep
trading through turn 15, ironic defenses of the mother alternating with
fresh mockery, and the evaluation is never settled. The contrast with A1
is not that the human thread lacks a consensus but that its consensus
stays available for reopening. Post and account identifiers are withheld
under the policy of §8; H1 is an internal label.
